The diary keeps your measurements (blood pressure, pulse, sugar, weight, temperature, oxygen) and your list of medicines, then builds a report that you can send to your doctor in a messenger. The app gives no medical advice.
1. Open the Medicines tab and add your medicines: name, dose, when to take.\n2. Open the Readings tab and tap + to enter your first measurement.

Choose the measurement type and the time of day (morning or evening). Type the values, or tap the microphone icon at the right of a field and say the number. You can also dictate a whole phrase into the quick entry field, for example: "pressure 135 over 80 pulse 72" — the fields fill in by themselves. Tick the medicines you have taken and tap Save.

Every input field has a microphone icon at the right. It opens the speech recognition of your phone. Say numbers in digits or in words. For decimals (sugar, weight, temperature) say five point five, five comma five or 5 and 5, and you get 5.5. If a measurement type is already chosen, you can skip its name in the quick entry field: just say four point two. If your phone has no speech recognition, use the microphone key on your keyboard. Always check the recognized value before saving.

The Readings tab shows entries as a table. Pick the measurement type at the top. If the table is wider than the screen, swipe it left or right. Units are shown in the column headers, the cells hold only values. The pencil edits an entry, the bin deletes it. The Clear button under the table deletes all entries of the chosen type at once, after you confirm. The Medicines tab works the same way: a table with the Clear button under it.

On the To doctor tab enter your name, choose the period and tap Send to doctor. Pick a messenger (Telegram, WhatsApp, MAX, e-mail and so on) and then the doctor. The Copy button copies the report text.
Theme: system, light or dark. Language: system, Russian or English. All data is stored only on this phone and is lost if the app is deleted, so send the report to your doctor regularly.

The top bar shows the app name and what the current tab holds. The three-dot menu on the right gives quick access to: a new reading, sending to the doctor, this guide, settings and information about the app.
